title: Platform-wide slowness and 429s
executive_summary: Latency and 429 errors start at ~19:55-20:00Z, when request volume into api-gateway, user-service and auth-service roughly doubled-to-tripled. Logs attribute the surge to client_id=mobile-ios-7.4.0, which is reported as the top client by RPS and whose requests are mostly retries that ignore Retry-After. The gateway's rate limiter then returns 429s, which likely drive further retries. The user-service release 7.1.3 (19:48Z) does not match the symptom pattern: its latency and error metrics are flat, and the traffic onset came after it. The most likely cause is a retry storm from the mobile-ios 7.4.0 client, not the user-service deployment.

hypotheses.description: Retry storm from mobile-ios-7.4.0 clients that ignore Retry-After, saturating api-gateway and downstream auth/user services and triggering 429s. Mechanism: A mobile client version (7.4.0) retries aggressively and ignores Retry-After. Request rate rose from ~1.2k to ~4k rps at the gateway starting 19:55Z. Gateway CPU rose from ~34% to ~90%, which drives 429s and latency. Downstream auth-service and user-service request rates rose ~2.2x and their CPU rose to 75-86%, while their own error and timeout rates stayed flat. Retry traffic continues because Retry-After is ignored.

probable_root_cause.description: Retry storm from mobile-ios-7.4.0 clients that ignore Retry-After, saturating api-gateway and downstream auth/user services and triggering 429s.
probable_root_cause.label: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed)

root_cause_statement: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed): traffic_surge in api-gateway - Retry storm from mobile-ios-7.4.0 clients that ignore Retry-After, saturating api-gateway and downstream auth/user services and triggering 429s.
corrective_actions: Throttle or block mobile-ios-7.4.0 at the gateway, or enforce Retry-After server-side, to stop the retry loop
Scale api-gateway and auth/user-service capacity temporarily if the throttle is not enough
Coordinate with mobile team on a hotfix or forced upgrade for client 7.4.0
preventive_actions: Enforce server-side backoff and per-client quotas at the gateway, and reject clients that ignore Retry-After
Add client version-aware rate limits and canary rollout for mobile releases
Add contract tests and client-behaviour tests for retry policy
monitoring_recommendations: Alert on per-client retry ratio and requests per client_id at the gateway
Alert on gateway request rate deviating more than 50% from baseline
limitations: No client-side or app release telemetry was available
The per-client RPS log values are inconsistent with total gateway RPS
Postgres and redis metrics were not queried
Log summaries were sampled and may be incomplete
[agent-reported gap] Source of the initial traffic increase at 19:55Z (client release vs. external trigger) is not confirmed
[agent-reported gap] No user-service logs were pulled for the 19:48Z deploy window
[agent-reported gap] No postgres metrics for the report_rollup period
Confidence values are rule-based evidence-strength scores, not calibrated probabilities.
conclusion: The incident is most consistent with a retry storm from mobile-ios-7.4.0 clients that ignore Retry-After. It began at ~19:55Z, which precedes the 429s and the latency and CPU rise. The user-service 7.1.3 deploy at 19:48Z is not supported by the metrics. Confidence is moderate because the per-client RPS figures are internally inconsistent, and the client release data was not available. The final status is PROBABLE_ROOT_CAUSE.
